source: Published evidence of an agent's review of one integration diff, an epic's review pull request or a hot-fix's delivering pull request, and its acceptance evidence.
- When a blocking finding or any hot-fix finding requires a fix:
- Blocking findings, and every finding on a hot-fix's delivering pull request, must be fixed and reviewed at the recorded head. Every finding has a completed disposition before handoff.

Write a JSON list containing the [Review Record](#review-record), with the full reviewed head and target SHAs, the `base_ref` a hot-fix's record carries, the scope actually inspected, findings and validation results. An empty findings list states that the review found no defect.

Each finding contains `description`, `severity` (`blocking` or `nonblocking`) and `disposition` (`open`, `fixed` or `deferred`). A fixed finding has an HTTPS `evidence` link; a deferred finding has an HTTPS `ticket` link. A record on a hot-fix's delivering pull request also carries `base_ref`, the name of its base branch. A record is current while it names the pull request's head and base SHAs. One on a hot-fix's delivering pull request is current while it names its head SHA and its base branch: its reviewed change is the head against its target, which a target moving on leaves as it was and a retarget does not. The last record for the same revision is authoritative.

Only an initiative, an epic or a hot-fix stands In Review. An open task issue is In Progress while a delivery pull request, draft or ready, links it, and Done once that pull request merges into the epic base and the issue closes as completed. Every jurisdiction refuses a task set In Review.
The queue for one theme board: initiative priority sets, hot-fix status, status and assignee changes, pending decisions, waiting work, next epics, Ready units and epics waiting on a priority.

- Refuse a Status change outside Backlog, Ready and In Progress, identifying the issue, other than a hot-fix’s, which its [Board Status](hotfix.md#board-status) settles. In Review, Done and task issues are otherwise outside the write scope.
- Each hot-fix stands where its [Board Status](hotfix.md#board-status) places it.

The queue contains calls for Status and assignee changes to initiatives, epics and hot-fixes. Status changes are between Backlog, Ready and In Progress, and a hot-fix's change as its [Board Status](hotfix.md#board-status) gives it. The assignee is the login assigned to work from Ready. Call files occupy the supplied output directory, for example `board/`. They describe proposed changes, not confirmation of live board state.
The supplied complete initiative and hot-fix pull request records, one JSON object per nonempty line at the local file path. eg `prs.json`
### Standalone Issues
A standalone issue sits on no board.
- **Hot-fix.**
A hot-fix works on the branch its [Branch](hotfix.md#branch) names.

The brief names the epic or hot-fix issue URL, task ids, Descriptions, covered acceptance criteria and the theme board carrying that issue's item. It includes each task branch, with the base it is cut from and the unit checkout where the session works on it, and the project checkout the session merges through.
The available units, held rows and hot-fixes, blocked work and merge candidates for one board.

A unit is one task row or tasks that name each other in Joins, as [Work Breakdown](epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) defines. A unit of rows comes only from an epic that is Ready or In Progress in the supplied board items: the plan offers no other row, and none other is held. A [hot-fix unit](#hot-fix-units) has no row. One unit is one session's work, delivered by one pull request into each epic base it changes. Its first task id and Description determine the planning-folder identity, which every row of the unit is reserved with, and with each epic base it changes its branch and worktree, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) names them. In an epic of several bases, the bases a unit changes are read from the [Component](work-item.md#component) declaration of the work-item file each free row links, in the engineering worktree. A unit with a row linking no work item changes every epic base, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) states for unplanned rows.
### Hot-fix Units
A hot-fix is a unit as its [Delivery Unit](hotfix.md#delivery-unit) states, with the branch, base and worktree its [Branch](hotfix.md#branch) names.

- A `unit` line names one session's tasks, its lane as `lane 2` or `unlaned`, Coverage and record folder, then a branch, base and worktree for each epic base it changes, separated by semicolons: `branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-main, base i07/e00/main, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-main; branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-workflows, base i07/e00/workflows, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-workflows`. One base keeps the unsuffixed branch: `branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan, base i07/e00/main, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan`. A hot-fix's line names its prefix and issue: `unit F00 #874: unlaned, coverage AC1, record 2026-10-06-874-f00-key-validation, branch f00-key-validation, base workspace, worktree .worktrees/f00-key-validation`.

- An `undeclared` line names a row of a unit in an epic of several bases whose linked work item names no long-lived branch with an epic base, and why: the file is unread, or its component names no long-lived branch or one with no epic base. The unit is not offered until its work item declares one, and a run meeting one exits nonzero. It also names an open hot-fix, whatever its state, whose body names no [target](hotfix-body.md#target), or one of the project checkout's repository whose target the evaluated revision's [Branches](delivery-branches.md#branches) does not declare. It is offered as no unit and no merge until its target is one.
- A `hold` line names a row a session holds and the record it links, or a hot-fix its [Delivery Unit](hotfix.md#delivery-unit) holds.

- A `merge` line names an open pull request, never a draft, whose test plan has passed and the base it targets: a task pull request into an epic base, or an open hot-fix's [delivering pull request](hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) into its target, when no `undeclared` or unresolved line names that hot-fix's target.
- An `unrecorded` line names a hot-fix its [Delivery Unit](hotfix.md#delivery-unit) leaves unrecorded, and each merged delivering pull request.

- An unresolved hot-fix of a repository other than the project checkout's names its target, which that checkout's [Branches](delivery-branches.md#branches) cannot declare. It is offered once a plan whose project checkout is of its repository finds the target declared.

The optional JSON export holds exactly the available units in report order. Each entry has a repository-qualified `id`, its `record` folder and its complete `report` line. Joined rows share one entry, such as `o/r#I07:E00:W01+W02`; a hot-fix uses `o/r#F02`. Diagnostic, held and blocked lines remain in the report and create no export entry.

Check one selected unit immediately before execution and provide [Validated Unit](#validated-unit "●") to the requester, or [Failure](#failure "●") if the operation fails. The start names one selected unit, has a currently free harness slot and overlaps no held or running session. Its supplied evidence names that unit, the planning record confirmed on the remote engineering branch, and the record associated with its confirmed hold. For rows, that association is read from every live row reservation; for a hot-fix it is the run's record for the unit whose board hold was confirmed. The evidence is gathered in that order before execution; any missing, mismatched or unverified evidence blocks the start.

One run records its board identity, scope selectors and requested lane in a JSON object. The scope is the selected board (`["*"]`), or a list of repository-qualified initiative, epic, task or hot-fix identities, such as `o/r#I07`, `o/r#I07:E00`, `o/r#I07:E00:W01` or `o/r#F02`. Every row of a joined unit must fall within that scope. An explicit joined selector, `o/r#I07:E00:W01+W02`, authorizes both rows. The requested lane must meet [Index](lane.md#index), represented as `null` when none is requested. eg `{"board": "users/o/projectsV2/7", "scope": ["o/r#I07"], "lane": null}`

Its worktree is named by its branch, as a task branch's is.
A repository-qualified reference to the hot-fix's delivering pull request.

- A pull request delivers a hot-fix when its title opens with the hot-fix's prefix, `[F00] Purpose`, it lives in the hot-fix's repository, its base is the hot-fix's [target](hotfix-body.md#target), and its Development field links the hot-fix.

- A reopened hot-fix still counts a delivering pull request merged before it reopened, since the issue records no reopen time.

Delivery requires both the user's authorization for the selected target and the harness capability to execute its mutation. A task targets its [epic base](delivery-branches.md#epic-bases); an epic targets that base's long-lived branch; a hot-fix uses task delivery against its declared long-lived target. The allowance for an epic base supplies no permission for another target. A merge into the default branch stays with a person. Another target requiring a person's approving review stays with that reviewer. A target without that requirement can be merged only within the authorization and harness permission actually granted for it. Neither the skill nor a ready result expands those grants or authorizes a protection bypass.
